data.body_html:
Experience the magic of the Mediterranean on a Marbella dolphin watching brunch cruise 2043. Departing from Puerto Banús at 10:00, this 2-hour morning voyage takes you into the open sea to spot wild dolphins in their natural habitat – all while enjoying a fresh brunch and drinks on board.

Why choose this cruise?

This is not a crowded tour boat. You charter the entire Azimut 39 – a 12.5m motor yacht – for your private group of up to 11 guests. The early start means calmer seas and higher chances of dolphin activity. The route heads west along the coast towards Cabopino, where bottlenose and common dolphins frequently feed near the underwater canyons.

What’s included in the brunch

Your brunch features a selection of fresh pastries, seasonal fruit, yoghurt, and a platter of local cheeses and cured meats. Drinks flow freely: water, soft drinks, beer, white wine, and cava. Everything is included in the price – no hidden extras.

Boat details: Azimut 39

  • Length: 12.5m
  • Capacity: 11 guests
  • Departs from: Puerto Banús
  • Features: Flybridge, sunbathing area, shaded salon, onboard WC
  • Skipper: Licensed and experienced

Price and value

At €749 for the whole boat (2 hours), this works out to just €68 per person for a group of 11. Compare that to mass-market dolphin tours charging €50–70 per person for a crowded boat – here you get privacy, flexibility, and a premium brunch.

Best months for dolphin sightings

Dolphins are present year-round in the Alboran Sea, but sightings peak from May to October. Water temperatures rise, and baitfish schools attract pods of up to 50 dolphins. Our skippers monitor local conditions and know the hotspots off Marbella and Estepona.

What to expect on the day

Meet at Puerto Banús at 09:45. Board the Azimut 39, meet your skipper, and receive a safety briefing. Cast off at 10:00. Cruise west at 20 knots, scanning the horizon for splashes and dorsal fins. Once dolphins are spotted, the skipper slows down for close-up viewing (keeping a respectful distance). Brunch is served while you watch. Return to Puerto Banús at 12:00.

Other experiences you might like

If you prefer a longer day on the water, consider our Marbella sunset charter or a full-day exploration to Estepona. For a more exclusive outing, the luxury yacht charter offers a larger vessel with more amenities.

Frequently asked questions

How long is the Marbella dolphin watching brunch cruise?

The cruise lasts 2 hours, from 10:00 to 12:00. This is enough time to reach the dolphin feeding grounds off Cabopino and return to Puerto Banús.

What is included in the brunch?

Your brunch includes fresh pastries, fruit, yoghurt, and a selection of local cheeses and meats. Drinks include water, soft drinks, beer, white wine, and cava – all included in the price.

Which boat is used for this cruise?

We use the Azimut 39, a 12.5m motor yacht that carries up to 11 guests. It has a spacious flybridge for panoramic views and a shaded salon.

How much does it cost?

The price is €749 for the entire boat (up to 11 guests) for 2 hours. This includes skipper, fuel, brunch, drinks, insurance, and 21% VAT.

Do you guarantee dolphin sightings?

We cannot guarantee sightings as dolphins are wild animals. However, our skippers know the best areas off Cabopino and Estepona, and sightings are very common from May to October.

Can I book for a private group?

Yes, the entire boat is yours. You can bring up to 11 guests. No other groups join the cruise.

What should I bring?

Bring sunscreen, sunglasses, a hat, and a light jacket for the morning breeze. Cameras are recommended for dolphin photos.

How do I book?

Contact us via WhatsApp for availability and booking. Payment is required in advance to secure your slot.
